newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall as investors eye wholesale inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall as investors eye wholesale inflation data.

text.p: Stock prices closed lower Thursday as investors kept a low profile ahead of Friday's release of wholesale price data for March.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 23.79 points at 6,540.05. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,307 to 1,092 on moderate volume of 421 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"I think we're in a bit of a holding pattern here," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities. For the second day, technology and financial stocks led the market lower.
With investors awaiting the Producer Price Index, stocks tracked a tentative performance by the bond market.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 3/32, while its yield edged up to 7.11 percent from Wednesday's close of 7.10 percent.
Analysts said the cautious atmosphere would likely put a cap on any near-term gains in stocks.
"The sentiment is pretty negative here," said Peter Green, director of technical research at Gruntal & Co. "If we do go higher, it's going to be met with selling."
The pessimism was evident in a report that showed new investment in mutual funds fell sharply last month.
According to the Investment Company Institute, a mutual fund trade group, new cash flowing to stock mutual funds slowed to an estimated $9.5 billion in March from $18.45 billion inflow in February.
It said the March figure was the lowest since July, 1996, a month that also saw the stock market endure a significant correction.
The mounting pessimism had some analysts wondering if the market was nearing a bottom.
"I think there was an excess of caution over the last couple of weeks," Farley said. Citing technology stocks in particular, she said, "Some of them look very buyable now."
The group, however, was among the weakest in Thursday's session. Intel Corp. fell 5 to 137-1/4 and Microsoft Corp. dipped 1-1/4 to 96-3/4.

Among bank stocks, which continued to lead the market in its day-to-day gyrations, Citicorp fell 2-3/4 to 110-1/8, Chase Manhattan Corp. lost 1-3/8 to 94-1/8 and Wells Fargo & CoC was off 5-1/2 to 270-1/2.
Retailers turned in a mixed performance after reporting their monthly sales figures.
Among the most active issues in the group were Wal-Mart Stores Inc., which fell 1/4 to 28-3/8 and K Mart Corp., unchanged at 12-1/2.
Sears, Roebuck & Co. slid 3-5/8 to 47-1/4 after announcing it would refund some payments from credit card holders who had filed for bankruptcy. Sears could not say how much it expected to repay.
Microcom Inc. surged 5-7/16 to 15-15/16 after it reached agreement to be acquired by Compaq Computer Corp. for 16-1/4 a share, or about $280 million. Compaq fell 2-3/4 to 75-3/.
Primark Corp. fell 5-1/4 to 18-3/4 after the information technology company warned its first quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' estimates.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 13.66 points to 1,235.77.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 2.26 points to 758.34. The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.21 to 563.19.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.93 to 399.36. The average share was down 9 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,238.132 down 30.433 or 0.42 percent.
